correctness.rationale: Every diametral pair of a compact convex polytope comprises vertices, since Euclidean squared norm is strictly convex separately in endpoints. For a fixed ordered diametral (v,w), e=(w-v)/L has positive pairing with every nonzero inward tangent direction at v; the diameter inequality yields strict positivity. Boundary facets near v are exact k=d-1 homogeneous cones, so the normalized axial deficit cap is exactly B(v,w)*t^k for small t. Two independent axial deficits convolve via a beta integral to (k!)^2/(2k)! B(v,w)B(w,v)*t^(2k). Euclidean chord deficit differs by O((norm h+norm j)^2), and strict axial positivity forces both of order epsilon, leading to O(epsilon^(2k+1)) correction. Finiteness of diametral ordered vertices permits summation and positive universal exponent 2d-2. Facet simplex cone computation yields for regular simplex d(d+1)4^(d-2)((d-1)!)²/(2d-2)! and cube 2^(d-2)d^(d-1)/(2d-2)!, with d3 constants 8 and 3/4. Independently evaluated exact factorial constants d=3,4,5 and source verify.py, which contains exact cone diagnostics and Monte Carlo importance tests. The all-polytope theorem rests on geometric cone proof, not simulations.
